Aleph.title: Opening the Hebrew Doorway
Aleph.goal: Start Hebrew at the right edge and move toward the left.
practice: Place a start mark at the right edge; trace a path toward the left.
Take turns pointing to the Hebrew start and saying the direction aloud.

Aleph.title: Hebrew Letters Are Not English Letters
Aleph.goal: Recognize that Hebrew has its own letter shapes and names.
practice: Sort Hebrew letters and Latin letters into separate groups.
Choose one Hebrew letter; point to it and say its name after a teacher model.

Aleph.title: The Hebrew Side of the Page
Aleph.goal: Track a Hebrew line from right to left, one word at a time.
practice: Track a whole line from right to left with your finger.
Pause at the space between words, then continue from the next word on the right.

Aleph.title: Aleph: The First Silent Carrier
Aleph.goal: Aleph carries a vowel mark in these examples; hear the modeled ahhh sound without adding an Aleph consonant.
practice: Circle Patach and box Qamatz.
Point to א then the mark below; say ahhh for אַ and אָ.

Aleph.title: Ayin: Another Silent Carrier
Aleph.goal: Ayin is a distinct letter; use a gentle class pronunciation and respect tradition differences.
practice: Match עַ and עָ to the two ahhh marks.
Practice the teacher’s pronunciation model and listen respectfully to other traditions.

Aleph.title: Silent Carriers Review: Aleph and Ayin
Aleph.goal: Recognize Aleph and Ayin, then pair them with the two ahhh marks.
practice: Sort Aleph and Ayin letter cards.
Pair each letter with a Stick Vowel and explain which part gives the sound.

Aleph.title: Bet and Vet: The Dot Matters
Aleph.goal: Distinguish Bet’s inside dot from Vet’s open center; learn the Pea Vowel beneath the letter.
practice: Circle the Bet ball and underline the Pea below.
Read בִּ and בִ after naming the inside dot and the beneath dot.

Aleph.title: Dagesh Practice: Seeing Before Saying
Aleph.goal: Notice the dagesh dot inside a letter before saying its modeled consonant sound.
practice: Find which examples have a dot inside.
Compare בּ/ב and כּ/כ; echo the community sound model.

Aleph.title: Bet in Simple Words and Names
Aleph.goal: Read two Bet examples that use the previously taught ahhh marks.
practice: Cover the meanings and read בַּת and בָּא from right to left.
Uncover the gloss; tell which word means daughter and which means came.

Aleph.title: Mem and Final Mem: A Letter with an Ending Form
Aleph.goal: Recognize Mem in its regular form and its final form at a word’s end.
practice: Match מ with ם and find each in a letter row.
Place ם only in the ending box.

Aleph.title: Shin and Sin: The Dot’s Place Matters
Aleph.goal: The right-side dot cues Shin; the left-side dot cues Sin.
practice: Mark the side of each dot before naming Shin or Sin.
Sort the sh and s forms; read only after checking the dot.

Aleph.title: Lamed: The Tall Letter
Aleph.goal: Recognize Lamed by its tall stroke and blend it with known ahhh vowels.
practice: Find Lamed among short letters.
Trace ל, then blend לַ and לָ.

Aleph.title: The Dot Over and Vav-Cholam: Oh
Aleph.goal: Cholam is the dot over a letter; Vav-Cholam carries the oh sound.
practice: Point to the dot over the letter in בֹּ and name oh.
Find the dot over Vav in בוֹ and compare the two oh patterns.

Aleph.title: Vav: The Connecting Letter
Aleph.goal: Recognize Vav in its upright shape and in a familiar vowel pattern.
practice: Find Vav in a mixed letter row.
Compare ו with י; name which one is taller.

Aleph.title: Yod: Small but Important
Aleph.goal: Recognize Yod as a small but important letter.
practice: Find Yod without relying on its place in a row.
Trace י and blend יַ using the already taught Patach.

Aleph.title: Hey: A Letter with Breath
Aleph.goal: Recognize Hey by its open shape and gentle breath sound.
practice: Point to the opening in Hey.
Compare ה and ח; use the class sound model for each.

Aleph.title: Name-Building Review and the Three Eggs
Aleph.goal: Recognize Yod, Vav, and Hey; introduce Segol, the Three Eggs eh vowel.
practice: Compare Yod, Vav, and Hey by size and opening.
Count the three Segol dots; read בֶּ and מֶ as eh.

Aleph.title: Dalet and Resh: Careful Corners
Aleph.goal: Compare Dalet and Resh by their small corner and stroke differences.
practice: Place ד and ר side by side.
Trace the corner detail slowly; identify each letter in a mixed row.

Aleph.title: Kaf, Khaf, and Final Kaf
Aleph.goal: Distinguish Kaf, Khaf, and final Kaf; the dot and final position matter.
practice: Sort כּ, כ, and ך by dot and word position.
Keep the final form in the ending box and echo the Khaf model.

Aleph.title: Final Forms Family I: Mem, Nun, Kaf
Aleph.goal: Match Mem, Nun, and Kaf with their final forms.
practice: Match each middle form with its final partner.
Write one family pair and explain where the ending shape belongs.

Aleph.title: Final Forms Family II: Pey and Tsadi
Aleph.goal: Match Peh and Tsadi with their final forms.
practice: Match פ/ף and צ/ץ.
Sort regular and final forms, then read the letter names.

Aleph.title: Final Forms Review: The Ending Doorway
Aleph.goal: Review all five final letter shapes and place each at a word’s end.
practice: Place all five final forms in ending boxes.
Say each family name and show its regular partner.

Aleph.title: Chet: A Strong New Sound
Aleph.goal: Recognize Chet as a distinct letter and learn its pronunciation from the teacher.
practice: Find ח among Hey and other shapes.
Listen to the teacher’s pronunciation and echo at a comfortable level.

Aleph.title: Tet and Tav: Similar Sounds, Different Letters
Aleph.goal: Recognize Tet and Tav as different letters, even when both represent t.
practice: Find ט and ת in a mixed row.
Name the shape before saying a sound; both may use t in the class tradition.

Aleph.title: The OOOH Vowel Pair: Kubutz and Vav-Shuruk
Aleph.goal: Kubutz is the three-dot staircase “OOOH belly”; Vav with its middle dot (Shuruk) also says oo.
practice: Count the three Kubutz dots in בֻ and trace their staircase.
Point to the dot inside וּ in בוּ; compare the two oo patterns.

Aleph.title: Qof: The Letter Below the Line
Aleph.goal: Recognize Qof by its descending shape and learn its class pronunciation.
practice: Trace ק and point to its descending feature.
Compare Qof with Kaf and say which one drops below.

Aleph.title: Samekh and Zayin: Visual Precision
Aleph.goal: Compare the rounded shape of Samekh with the angled shape of Zayin.
practice: Sort rounded ס and angled ז.
Find each shape in a mixed row and name it.

Aleph.title: Gimel: Returning to a Distinct Shape
Aleph.goal: Recognize Gimel by its distinct shape and modeled g sound.
practice: Find ג among similar letters.
Trace Gimel and say its class-model sound.

Aleph.title: Review by Family: Quiet, Dotted, Final
Aleph.goal: Sort carrier, dotted, and final-form families.
practice: Sort א/ע, בּ/ב, and מ/ם into the named families.
Explain one clue used in every group.

Aleph.title: Review by Shape: Tall, Small, Closed, Confusing
Aleph.goal: Use tall, small, open, closed, and corner features to identify letters.
practice: Sort letters by tall, small, open, closed, and corner features.
Name the specific letter after pointing to its shape clue.

Aleph.title: Simple Word: Or — Light
Aleph.goal: Decode אוֹר and connect it to light; Vav-Cholam was taught earlier.
practice: Cover the gloss and picture; decode אוֹר.
Uncover the meaning and explain which mark cues oh.

Aleph.title: Simple Word: Shalom
Aleph.goal: Decode שָׁלוֹם and connect it to hello or peace.
practice: Decode שָׁלוֹם before saying its meaning.
Use it as hello or peace in a teacher-modeled example.

Aleph.title: Simple Word: Bayit
Aleph.goal: Decode בַּיִת and connect it to house.
practice: Read בַּיִת without a picture.
Tell which familiar vowel mark helps with the second beat.

Aleph.title: Names and Hebrew Letters
Aleph.goal: Read Hebrew names from their letters and taught vowel marks.
practice: Read דָּוִד and מֹשֶׁה from the Hebrew letters.
Point to a vowel mark already studied before saying each name.

Aleph.title: Aleph Track Readiness Review
Aleph.goal: Show recognition of letters, marks, and familiar words without picture guessing.
practice: Name one letter family, one vowel pattern, and one short word.
Read a short example aloud and explain the steps, not just the meaning.

Aleph.title: Celebration of Beginning
Aleph.goal: Reflect on growth and choose a comfortable next learning step.
practice: Choose a letter or word you can now read more confidently.
Tell a teacher one thing you learned and one thing you want to practice next.

Bet.title: Blend ahhh and eee
Bet.goal: Blend a familiar consonant and vowel without guessing a whole word.
practice: Read each small sound before blending the whole word.
Point to the mother and father in the picture. Read their labels.
Say each word again without using the picture to guess.

Bet.title: Close a word with a consonant
Bet.goal: Read the final consonant without adding an extra vowel.
practice: Touch the rightmost letter first.
Blend the vowel, then finish with m or d.
Use the sea and hand picture to check meaning after reading.

Bet.title: Read the over vowel oh
Bet.goal: Recognize both common oh spellings and blend a word for light.
practice: Find the dot above in each model.
Blend oh and r. Finish with r, without an added vowel.
Read the word, then point to the light in the picture.

Bet.title: Read the belly vowel oo
Bet.goal: Read both oo patterns and decode two pictured words.
practice: Find the belly dot and the three-dot staircase.
Read the word before using the picture.
Point to the horse or a strawberry to show meaning.

Bet.title: Read eh and ay carefully
Bet.goal: Distinguish the three eggs from the two side-by-side dots.
practice: Point to each vowel and say eh or the class ay cue.
Read bread slowly, joining the last m without adding a vowel.
Read son with your teacher: class bayn; often ben in modern Hebrew.

Bet.title: Read a greeting with meaning
Bet.goal: Blend known patterns into shalom and two short greetings.
practice: Read shalom without a picture hint.
Read each greeting, then tell whom you greeted.
Act out one greeting with a study partner.

Bet.title: Meet Gimel in a fish word
Bet.goal: Recognize Gimel and blend it with a familiar final consonant.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: dag.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Compare son and daughter
Bet.goal: Recognize final Nun and distinguish two short family words by their final consonants.
practice: Read the vowel and consonant sounds before you name the family word.
Compare the last letter in בֵּן and בַּת.
Say both words again without picture hints.

Bet.title: Read Peh in פֶּה
Bet.goal: Read Peh with its inside dot and recognize the word for mouth.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: peh.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read Tet in טוֹב
Bet.goal: Recognize Tet and blend a familiar oh sound with Vet.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: tov.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Build a two-beat dog word
Bet.goal: Blend two familiar syllables into one word without guessing from the picture.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: ke-lev.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Meet Zayin in זֶה
Bet.goal: Recognize Zayin and read a short word meaning this.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: zeh.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read a tree word with final Tsadi
Bet.goal: Notice the final form Tsadi and close the word without adding a vowel.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: etz.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Hear Qof in קוֹל
Bet.goal: Recognize Qof and decode a word for voice or sound.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: kol.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read Lamed in לֵב
Bet.goal: Use the ay vowel cue to read a one-beat word for heart.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: lev.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read Nun in נֵר
Bet.goal: Blend Nun with the ay vowel cue and finish with Resh.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: ner.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read small: קָטָן
Bet.goal: Decode a two-beat describing word and attend to its vowel marks.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: ka-tan.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read big: גָּדוֹל
Bet.goal: Blend three familiar consonants and two vowel sounds into a describing word.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: ga-dol.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read a familiar day word
Bet.goal: Read יוֹם as one word and hear its final Mem.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: yom.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Blend the two beats in מַיִם
Bet.goal: Read a two-beat word and keep both syllables in order.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: ma-yim.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read the repeated sun word
Bet.goal: Notice a repeated syllable pattern while decoding a familiar two-beat word.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: she-mesh.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read a city word
Bet.goal: Blend the hiriq sound with familiar Yud and Resh.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: ir.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read the word for head
Bet.goal: Use the over vowel and familiar Shin to decode a one-beat word.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: rosh.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read a book and a describing word
Bet.goal: Read a two-word phrase and notice that Hebrew places the describing word after the noun.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: sefer tov.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Compare house and garden
Bet.goal: Read two place words and compare their different lengths and endings.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: bayit · gan.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Compare big and small
Bet.goal: Use vowel marks and known vocabulary to distinguish two opposites.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: gadol · katan.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Ask מָה זֶה?
Bet.goal: Read a simple question using two familiar words.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: mah zeh?.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Answer with זֶה סֵפֶר
Bet.goal: Read a simple identification phrase and connect it to an object.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: zeh sefer.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read an object with a friend
Bet.goal: Practice a noun and a familiar describing word as a phrase.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: kelev gadol.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read a small fish phrase
Bet.goal: Combine a familiar noun with a describing word and preserve word order.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: dag katan.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read family words without picture clues
Bet.goal: Use vowels and final consonants to identify familiar family words independently.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: abba · imma · ben · bat.
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Bet.title: Read the Bet Track mini passage
Bet.goal: Read a short set of linked phrases and explain what each one means.
practice: Point to the rightmost letter first, then move left as you read.
Say the word or phrase aloud: mah zeh? zeh dag. dag katan..
Tell the meaning in your own words, then check the picture.

Gimel.title: Reading with Meaning
Gimel.goal: See the letters, read the word from right to left, then explain its meaning.
practice: Point to each letter in אוֹר. Read or first; look for light only after you have decoded it.

Gimel.title: Notice the Sun Word
Gimel.goal: Read from the first letter on the right. Let the two syllables stay clear: she-mesh.
practice: Point to each letter as you read; then cover the picture and tell what the word means.

Gimel.title: Read a Hand Word
Gimel.goal: Blend the vowel and finish with ד, Dalet. Do not add an extra vowel after the last letter.
practice: Touch the final letter only after you have read the vowel.

Gimel.title: Read a Sea Word
Gimel.goal: Read right to left and close the word with final Mem, ם.
practice: Stretch the vowel briefly, then close with m.

Gimel.title: Read Water in Two Beats
Gimel.goal: Hear the word in two beats: ma-yim. The final ם keeps its m sound.
practice: Say both beats, then blend them into one word.

Gimel.title: Read a House Word
Gimel.goal: Read the Bet first, then follow the vowel pattern toward Tav. The word names a place to live.
practice: Read before looking at the picture. Point to a house only after you say the word.

Gimel.title: Read a Bread Word
Gimel.goal: Read the two parts slowly, then close with ם. Follow your teacher’s model for ח.
practice: Do not guess from the picture; use the letters and vowels first.

Gimel.title: Read a Strawberry Word
Gimel.goal: The two ת letters frame the oo sound. Keep the word short and clear.
practice: Point to the middle vowel, then say the first and last sounds.

Gimel.title: Compare Sea and Hand
Gimel.goal: The first letter and vowel are alike. The final consonant changes the word’s meaning.
practice: Read both words, then point to the final letter that makes them different.

Gimel.title: Ask Who?
Gimel.goal: This short word asks about a person. Read it as one smooth syllable.
practice: Ask “מִי?” and invite a partner to answer with a person’s name.

Gimel.title: Use a Greeting
Gimel.goal: Read the parts sha-lom. The same greeting can open or close a conversation.
practice: Say shalom to a partner, then use it again when you part.

Gimel.title: Read Mother
Gimel.goal: Use the class pronunciation model. Read the whole word before connecting it to a person.
practice: Say the word gently, then point to the matching family picture.

Gimel.title: Read Father
Gimel.goal: Notice the repeated sound pattern. Read both syllables without rushing.
practice: Read the word, then use it in a greeting: שָׁלוֹם אַבָּא.

Gimel.title: Read Son
Gimel.goal: Start at Bet and finish with final Nun, ן. The last form changes shape, not sound.
practice: Find ן at the end and keep its n sound.

Gimel.title: Read a Book Word
Gimel.goal: Read the vowel under Samech, then the two syllables. Follow your teacher’s pronunciation for Peh.
practice: Read the word first. Then choose a book and say סֵפֶר.

Gimel.title: Read Child
Gimel.goal: Read both short syllables and finish with Dalet. A word can name a person.
practice: Say the word, then show the picture that matches it.

Gimel.title: Read Girl
Gimel.goal: Compare this word with יֶלֶד. Notice how a different ending can change the word.
practice: Read both words aloud with a teacher, then sort the matching pictures.

Gimel.title: Read Heart
Gimel.goal: The final ב without a dot is read as v in this word. Keep the final sound soft.
practice: Read the word, then connect “heart” to a feeling or kind action.

Gimel.title: Read Friend
Gimel.goal: Follow the teacher’s model for ח. Read both syllables before naming the relationship.
practice: Read the word, then use it to greet a friend.

Gimel.title: Read Good
Gimel.goal: The over vowel gives oh here. Finish with Bet, which is soft after the vowel.
practice: Read טוֹב, then use it with a picture or object you like.

Gimel.title: Read Day
Gimel.goal: Read the whole word as one beat. Final Mem closes the word.
practice: Say יוֹם and point to a picture of daytime.

Gimel.title: Read Song
Gimel.goal: Find the dot on the right side of ש for Shin. Read the vowel and finish with Resh.
practice: Read the word, then hum a short tune you know.

Gimel.title: Read Voice
Gimel.goal: The Qof begins the word. Read the oh pattern and close with Lamed.
practice: Say קוֹל softly and loudly; notice that the meaning stays the same.

Gimel.title: Read Flower
Gimel.goal: Read the first syllable, then follow the vowel under Resh. Use your teacher’s model for ח.
practice: Trace the word from right to left and match it to a flower.

Gimel.title: Read Bird
Gimel.goal: The first letter is Tsadi. Read all three parts slowly, then blend them.
practice: Point to each sound. Use the picture only after you have decoded the word.

Gimel.title: Read Tree
Gimel.goal: The final form ץ is Tsadi at the end of a word. Its shape changes, but its sound remains.
practice: Find the final letter and say its sound without adding a vowel.

Gimel.title: Read King
Gimel.goal: Final Kaf ך appears at the end. The small sheva here closes the word; follow the teacher’s model.
practice: Read the word, then point to final ך. Do not add another syllable.

Gimel.title: Read Silver
Gimel.goal: Kaf begins the word and final Peh ף closes it. A final letter keeps its familiar sound.
practice: Find the two letters with changed or dotted forms, then read the word.

Gimel.title: Read Land
Gimel.goal: The word ends with final Tsadi ץ. Read to the end without adding an extra vowel.
practice: Point to the final form and compare it with צ at the start of צִפּוֹר.

Gimel.title: Say “This Is a Book”
Gimel.goal: Read each word, then join them. זֶה points to something nearby; סֵפֶר names it.
practice: Place a book nearby, point to it, and say זֶה סֵפֶר.

Gimel.title: Ask “What Is This?”
Gimel.goal: Read the question words together. Let your voice show that you are asking.
practice: Point to a familiar object and ask מַה זֶה? Let your partner answer.

Gimel.title: Read “I Have a Book”
Gimel.goal: Read the phrase in three parts. Keep the spaces between words, then say the whole idea.
practice: Hold a book and say the phrase. Then trade roles with a partner.
